headline: Reappointed three library trustees and reviewed programming, renovation, and policy updates.
summary: The board reviewed public comments about a newspaper sculpture article and the Declaration of Independence event, and discussed restoring the New York Times subscription at the Kingston Free Library. The director reported on staff promotions, the Community Learning Center project, and upcoming programs, and the board discussed a proposed Meeting Room Policy change that will be voted on in September.
decisions: The Town Council reappointed Liz Kroll, Mike Henry, and Bob Warren to the Library Board of Trustees.

decision_evidence.quote: The Town Council has reappointed Liz Kroll, Mike Henry and Bob Warren to the Board.

plain_text:
Town of South Kingstown   
Library Board of Trustees   
Regular Session Meeting Minutes 
Tuesday, August 11, 2026 at 6:00 PM   
Peace Dale Library 
Meeting Room 
1057 Kingstown Road, Peace Dale, RI 
www.southkingstownri.gov  
 
 
1. Call to Order & Roll Call: 
2. Approval of Minutes: 
 A. Regular Session — June 9, 2026 
3. Correspondence 
None 
4. Public Comment 
Elizabeth McNab brought up an article in the Providence Journal about the Weaver Sculpture outside the Peace Dale 
Library. There was also discussion about the Declaration of Independence event at the Kingston Free Library. 
Mike had been asked by a patron about the Sunday New York Times not being at the Kingston Free Library. Laurel stated 
it was previously purchased at Healy’s News, which has since closed. The subscription will be reactivated and delivered 
directly to the Kingston Free Library. 
5. President's Report 
Tim spoke on how proud he was of the staff’s work and dedication during the renovation period. Tim also reminded 
everyone of the upcoming Board elections at the September meeting. 
6. Director's Report 
Laurel has been elected as Vice-President of the Ocean State Libraries Executive Board. Karyn is attending the ASPEN 
online catalog meetings. 
Liz asked about the July Hazard Garden walk-through with the URI Master Gardener. Laurel reported nothing definite 
came out of the meeting, but the town is looking at seasonal staff to maintain it.Lindsay questioned the progress on the 
Peace Dale Library East doorway. Laurel reported it would be completed in time for the ceremony on August 25th. 
 A. Deputy Library Director position filled 
Karyn Leahy was introduced as the new Deputy Director. Tim thanked Karyn for her efforts with the Community 
Learning Center project. 
 B. Community Learning Center Coordinator vacany 
There are 10-12 candidates for the Community Learning Center vacancy created by Karyn’s promotion. Interviews will 
be conducted shortly. 
 C. Trustee Reappointments — Bob Warren, Mike Henry, Liz Kroll 
The Town Council has reappointed Liz Kroll, Mike Henry and Bob Warren to the Board.
7. Programming 
 A. Recaps 
• RI Declaration of Independence Exhibit 
• Firefighter Story time at Kingston Fire District 
• Summer Ready Kick-Off 
• Hale Library Annual Book Sale 
• *Children's programming has resumed at Peace Dale! 
 
The Declaration of Independence event went well. 
53 people attended the story time at the Kingston Fire District. 
56 people attended the Summer Kick-off event. 
Approximately $1600.00 dollars was raised at the Hale Branch book sale. 
  
 B. Upcoming 
• L.E.D. Mini Golf — Kingston Free, August 12th at10:30, 11:30, & 12:30 
• Evening Knitter & Crocheters Group — Robert Beverly Hale, Tuesday evenings at 6:00 
• Monuments & Memorials of South Kingstown — Kingston Free, August 26th at 6:00 
• Community Learning Center Ribbon Cutting — Peace Dale Library, August 25th at 11:00 
• Recycle Right in RI--Peace Dale Library, August 29th at 11:00 
  
8. Project and Grants Updates 
Community Learning Center 
 A. o Parking Lot 
o Hazard Garden 
o East Entryway 
o Ribbon Cutting — Tuesday, August 25th at 11:00 
 
  
The parking lot was repaved and striped and will get in depth paving with extra funds from grant. 
Hazard Garden will get interpretive signage and 5 restored benches, along with new fencing. 
Hilary asked if the Board could do anything for the ribbon cutting ceremony. Nothing needed at this time. 
9. Meeting Room Policy 
With the new spaces created in the Community Learning Center, Laurel feels the Meeting Room Policy will need to be 
adjusted. She and Karyn presented the staff’s proposal to the Board, with their reasons for the changes. The Board will 
review the proposal, and it will be on the September agenda for action. Staff have already seen an increase in requests 
for use since re-opening. 
10. Statistics 
Numbers are up since re-opening.
11. Next Meeting: 
September 8, 2026 
September 8, 2026 
12. Adjournment:
